title: Edamame + Feta Rice Salad
steps: Cook the rice: Rinse 1 cup white rice until the water runs clear. Combine with 1.5 cups water, bring to a boil, cover, and reduce to lowest heat. Cook undisturbed, then fluff onto a sheet pan and spread thin to cool fast.
Cool the rice: Spread the rice on a tray and leave it uncovered until fully room temperature. Don't skip this — warm rice wilts the herbs and melts the feta.
Tame the onion: Toss the sliced red onion with 1 tbsp of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Let it sit while you work — the acid strips the raw bite.

Blanch the edamame: Drop the frozen edamame into salted boiling water until tender and bright, then drain and run under cold water to stop the cooking. Drain hard — wet edamame waters down the dressing.
Make the dressing: Whisk together the olive oil, remaining lemon juice, lemon zest, salt, and black pepper until it thickens slightly.
Toss the salad: In a large bowl combine the cooled rice, edamame, cucumber, soaked onion, olives, dill, parsley, and mint. Pour over the dressing and toss thoroughly.
Fold in the feta: Add the crumbled feta and fold gently — three or four turns, no more. Scatter sunflower seeds on top. Taste and adjust salt and lemon; feta is salty, so season last.
notes: Protein per serving: edamame ~18g, feta ~8g, rice ~4g, about 30g in all; closer to 27g without the olives and seeds. The rice must be completely cool before it's dressed. Warm rice soaks up the oil and lemon instead of being coated by them, and the salad turns greasy and flat. The feta goes in last and gets folded, not stirred, or the whole bowl turns chalky.
freezeNote: The rice would freeze, but cucumber, fresh herbs, and feta don't. Make what gets eaten.
